title: Patients for Safety in Radiation Therapy (PASST!) A pilot study on the development and feasibility of needs-based patient information
summary:
Although patients play an important role in the safe delivery of radiotherapy, there is a lack of interventions that have been proven to strengthen patient competence in terms of patient safety. 
The planned study has three objectives: 
1) To develop information material that makes it easier for patients to participate in safe care
2) To review this material for usability and comprehensibility
3) To review the effect of the material on perceived safety

The study will be conducted in two phases, with patients and the treatment team working together.
Step 1: Develop the material (phase 1)
First, the informational material will be created. This will not be done at the desk of a single person, but in a kind of cycle (iterative process):
Topic search: The research group searches the available literature and asks patient representatives: “What do patients need to know to make therapy safer?”
Expert review: A team of experts then writes the texts.
Revision: The material is revised again in workshops with patients.
Comprehension test: Finally, 10 to 12 patients read the draft and give their honest opinion on whether they understand everything and whether it helps them in their everyday lives.
Step 2: The practical test (phase 2)
Before the material is distributed on a large scale, a small test run (feasibility study) is carried out:
Application: 20 patients receive the information before their first radiation treatment.
Feedback: Patients are asked via questionnaire and telephone interview: “Did it help you? Does it make you feel more confident?”
The goal of the project
The ultimate goal is to have information material that is tailored precisely to the needs of patients. If this small test is successful, the next step will be a large clinical study to scientifically prove that the information actually improves treatment in a measurable way.
conditions: The study is open for patient representers and patients with all tumors and medical staff.
